text:
The Anthropic/OpenAI "rogue AI agent" story escalated further today. Reuters and other outlets are now explicitly framing the upcoming Meta, Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI meeting with Trump administration officials as happening "amid rogue AI agent fallout." Anthropic pushed back publicly in the meantime -- Dark Reading covered its position that the Claude-driven attacks reflected security gaps in the target systems, not a problem with the model itself.

Alibaba kept pressing its challenge to US labs (Bloomberg: "Alibaba Adds to China AI Breakthroughs With New Qwen Model"). OpenAI had an eventful day of its own: it published a public rebuttal, "Apple is getting this wrong," pushing back on what it called a baseless lawsuit and correcting claims about its employees, while separately announcing new ChatGPT Work and Codex education plugins for K-12 and college use.

Agentic AI showed up as infrastructure and security news rather than just model releases: Hugging Face shipped LFM2.5-2.6B for deploying local agents "everywhere," NVIDIA released Alpamayo 2 Super, a frontier open model for robotaxis and autonomous vehicles, and NVIDIA-led SAFE guidelines for agentic AI cybersecurity transparency now have over 120 organizations behind them through the Open Secure AI Alliance. The Information also reported on Coinbase building its own coding agents to complement Anthropic's Claude Code, an example of enterprises building on top of frontier agent tooling rather than just consuming it.

On Hacker News, "LLMs reward expertise" was today's single biggest AI story (1,296 points), alongside a widely discussed piece on AI-generated images discouraging blog readership (706 points) -- both signal growing practitioner skepticism about how AI output gets used and perceived. Separately, a viral claim that AI companies are scanning and destroying millions of books, including rare titles, is currently being fact-checked by Snopes rather than confirmed.

No accepted-conference paper news or Hugging Face daily papers broke in the last 24 hours. The closest thing to a notable model release outside the frontier-lab announcements above was Mistral's Shieldstral, a 3B open-weights model for multimodal content moderation.
